commonErrors.why: You divide the mass by the speed. The amount of motion is a product of multiplication, not division.
You made a mistake in the number of zeros:. 1500 × 20 = 30000, not 300000.
You multiplied by the square of the speed or added the kinetic energy factor; The quantum of motion is linear in velocity and not quadratic.
You wrote the initial velocity. After coalescence, the mass tripled. The speed must decrease.
You divide by the mass of the moving object alone. After coalescence, the two masses move together, so the denominator is their sum.
You divide by the mass of the body at rest alone.
You added the two expressions, neglecting the sign of the second object : (12 + 10)/5 = 4.4. The second body moves to the left, so its momentum is negative and subtracted.
You missed the final sign. The momentum of the first 12 is greater than 10, so the resultant is positive and the movement is to the right.
You stopped at the total momentum +2.0 kg·m/s and did not divide it by the total mass.

questions.solution: J = F Δt = 200 × 0.050 = 10 N·s, which is equivalent to 10 kg·m/s in terms of momentum change.

commonErrors.why: You divided power by time. impulse is a product of multiplication; Dividing by time gives the rate of change of force, which is not what is required.
You wrote force. Thrust combines force and time, and its unit is N·s, not N.
You wrote time instead of impulse.

questions.solution: Before : ½(2.0)(6.0)² = 36 J. and after : ½(6.0)(2.0)² = 12 J. The missing 36 − 12 = 24 J turned into heat, distortion, and sound.

commonErrors.why: You assumed that kinetic energy is conserved. They are preserved in elastic collision alone; Coalition is the type of collision that loses the most energy. What is preserved here is the momentum, not the energy.
You wrote the energy before the collision, not the energy lost.
You wrote the energy after the collision, not the difference between them.
